::: {.about-text}
I'm a research scientist at the [ALERRT Center](https://alerrt.org) at Texas State University. I study the health and mortality of first responders, and, from the other side of the desk, how police officers are trained to make decisions and how the public judges the ones they make. My doctorate is in criminal justice, from the University of Cincinnati, which is where I learned why Texans don't own real winter coats. I came home for a postdoc in social genomics and epigenetics in the [Harden Lab](https://www.kpharden.com/) at UT Austin and have not left the I-35 corridor since.

Off the clock, I am:

- A husband and father of two little girls
- A native Texan (sixth generation, or thereabouts)
- A Brazilian jiu-jitsu black belt with passable skills — *ba dum tss*
- An academic nomad: criminology, then genomics, then population health
- An evangelical R user
- The worst *Cards Against Humanity* player you are likely to meet

The blog, [Left-hand Thoughts](../3_posts/posts.qmd), is where the overzealous applications of R to everyday problems end up. Posts are rare. I'm working on it.
